Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: revised complete Mosslight scene, correcting insufficient detail on the protagonist.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Image 2 is the ORIGINAL A REFERENCE and the required benchmark for character craftsmanship, face rendering, costume construction, material texture, and restrained pixel shading.
The user specifically rejected the previous B/C character faces and clothes as too simplified compared with original A. Make a clearly visible improvement in actual character detail. Re-render the protagonist carefully; generic sharpening, adding noise, thick outlines or changing colors is not an adequate edit.
Keep the entire target scene's composition and environment as closely unchanged as possible: architecture, roof, doors/windows, paths, pond, waterfall, dock, planting beds, lamp positions, plants, trees, props, background lighting, camera angle and framing. This pass corrects the protagonist, not the map. Keep their feet at the same ground position, the same overall character scale, full-body pose, recognizable identity and corrected A-like body proportions. The torso and short separated legs must remain readable. Do not inflate the head or shrink the body.
Character detail must be integrated naturally with the original A reference:
- Face: nuanced warm ivory skin in small deliberate pixel clusters; forehead and cheek planes, gentle hood-cast shadow, subtly modeled tiny nose and mouth, restrained blush rather than flat red circles. Small expressive dark eyes with distinct eyelid/upper edge and very small highlights, not blank black dot/oval stickers or oversized shiny anime eyes. Preserve the original cute, quiet, childlike face, not an adult face.
- Hair: individually separated short brown locks and irregular fringe, layered highlights and shadows, small side locks emerging from the hood; not a flat solid brown cap.
- Hood: clearly constructed fabric thickness, folded rim and inner lining, subtle seams and hand stitching, folds at crown, cheek opening and neck. Light should describe the material instead of a large smooth flat color patch.
- Clothes: distinguish outer cloak/coat from linen inner tunic and neck cloth. Show the scarf knot and folded tails, neckline closure, sleeve cuffs, overlapping cloth edges, shoulder and elbow folds, natural tunic drape and hem stitching. Use restrained fine fabric texture at the same pixel scale as A; not busy ornament or random speckles.
- Accessories: believable leather bag and strap with seam, flap edge and small buckle; leather boot openings, seams, toes and soles; a convincingly gripped lantern handle, fine brass frame and glass panes. Keep hand and finger indications simple, coherent and readable at this scale.
Use the original A's handcrafted, fine storybook pixel-art technique, selective colored outlines, stepped silhouettes, warm reflected lantern light and cool ambient shadows. Preserve the target palette identity. Increase detail density inside the existing silhouette, without making the figure giant, changing age, adding armor, jewellery, weapons or elaborate decorative embroidery.
Output one full-frame high-resolution landscape image with the same aspect and framing as image 1. Fine details should be genuinely drawn rather than simulated with blur, smooth airbrushing or a sharpen filter. No text, labels, inset panels, montage, border, logo or watermark.
B invariants: green/teal woodland and low round green cottage roof remain unchanged. The keeper keeps the ROUND SAGE-GREEN hood, peach neckerchief, sage outer cloak, creamy inner tunic, brown satchel, boots and warm handheld lantern. Match A's quality of cloth, hair and face rendering while preserving this B costume. No pointed purple hat or pompom.
